subject: [RFC PATCH 1/4] block: do not issue background swap bios as root

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Identified potential issue with using REQ_BACKGROUND to mark swap bios as non-urgent, suggesting that this could lead to throttling and foreground paging. The author agreed that zswap writebacks are best effort and can tolerate failure.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:18:36AM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> bio_issue_as_root_blkg() issues every REQ_SWAP bio as root, bypassing
> the cgroup IO controllers, because reclaim cannot stall indefinitely on
> swap writes. Some swap writes are not urgent though: zswap writeback is
> best effort.
> 
> Such a bio cannot simply drop REQ_SWAP: dm-crypt and dm-thin rely on it
> for limit_swap_bios, which caps in-flight swap bios to avoid a memory
> deadlock, see commit a666e5c05e7c ("dm: fix deadlock when swapping to
> encrypted device").

Is that true?  REQ_BACKGROUND very much implies the I/O can the throttled
and thus better not be foreground paging, and thus the caller should be
able to tolerate a failure.

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This patch series proposes a change to the block layer, specifically to the bio_issue_as_root_blkg() function. The goal is to prevent background swap bios from being issued as root, which bypasses cgroup IO controllers and can lead to memory deadlocks. This is done by introducing a new condition that checks for REQ_BACKGROUND in addition to REQ_SWAP.
